security_audit.summary: Most static matches are Markdown syntax or standard secret wiring. Confirmed risks include dynamic shell commands, expression injection, unsafe output handling, untrusted AI prompts, external data disclosure, and unauthorized rebasing.

remediation.issue: GitHub expressions enter executable shell and JavaScript source.
remediation.suggestion: Pass context through environment variables, parse it as data, and use collision-safe multiline output delimiters.

remediation.issue: Git commands interpolate unchecked refs and file values.
remediation.suggestion: Use execFile or spawn argument arrays and validate commit hashes, branch names, and paths.

remediation.issue: Public comments can trigger token-backed rebases.
remediation.suggestion: Require trusted author associations or explicit permissions, match commands exactly, and declare minimal job permissions.

remediation.issue: Untrusted repository content controls AI prompts and leaves the repository.
remediation.suggestion: Redact sensitive content, define data policies, isolate instructions, validate responses, and require human approval for consequential actions.

remediation.issue: Third-party actions use mutable major tags.
remediation.suggestion: Pin every action to a reviewed full commit SHA and use automated updates.

semantic_findings.title: Pull request data can inject JavaScript
semantic_findings.description: Changed files and diff output are inserted directly into github-script source, allowing repository content to alter privileged JavaScript.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow uses direct expression interpolation inside a JavaScript template literal while granting pull-request write permission.

semantic_findings.title: Changed filenames can inject shell syntax
semantic_findings.description: PR-controlled changed-file output is inserted directly into a shell loop, so crafted filenames can become executable shell syntax.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The step embeds a previous output into shell source instead of passing it through a quoted environment variable.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted content controls AI decisions
semantic_findings.description: Diffs, issue text, commit logs, and comments enter AI prompts without trust boundaries before outputs drive reviews, labels, checks, or comments.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Each example places repository-controlled text in an AI prompt and consumes the model response in an operational workflow.

semantic_findings.title: Repository content is sent to an external AI service
semantic_findings.description: The review workflow sends complete pull request diffs to Anthropic without redaction, content limits, or repository data policy checks.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code constructs an Anthropic request containing changed filenames and the complete diff.

semantic_findings.title: Any commenter can request a privileged rebase
semantic_findings.description: The rebase job checks only comment text, then uses a repository token to rebase and force-push without author authorization.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: No actor, association, or permission check appears between the public comment trigger and the write-capable Git commands.

semantic_findings.title: Actions use mutable version tags
semantic_findings.description: Workflow dependencies use movable major tags instead of reviewed commit SHAs, increasing supply-chain exposure if an upstream tag changes.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The uses entries visibly reference v4, v7, v9, and v1 tags rather than immutable commit identifiers.

content.value_statement: Manual reviews, triage, and repository maintenance consume engineering time. This skill provides adaptable GitHub Actions and TypeScript patterns for AI-assisted automation.
actual_capabilities: Draft GitHub Actions for AI-assisted pull request reviews and comments.
Define workflows for issue labeling and stale issue management.
Select tests from changed paths and add deployment risk checks.
Illustrate rebase, cherry-pick, rollback, and branch cleanup automation.
Configure CODEOWNERS and branch protection through GitHub APIs.
limitations: Several examples contain placeholders such as analyzeIssue, callAI, and ai.
The examples require security hardening before production use.
GitHub permissions, secrets, APIs, and repository policies require local configuration.
The skill does not execute workflows or verify repository compatibility.

use_cases.title: Automate pull request reviews
use_cases.description: Create an AI-assisted review workflow that summarizes changes and posts focused feedback.

use_cases.title: Optimize CI test selection
use_cases.description: Map changed paths to relevant test suites while retaining a complete fallback.

use_cases.title: Strengthen release operations
use_cases.description: Design approval, rollback, branch protection, and repository ownership workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Create issue triage
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a basic issue triage workflow. Use minimal permissions, approved labels, and clear secret requirements.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a repository with manual triage.

prompt_templates.title: Design AI pull request review
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an AI pull request review workflow for [repository]. Treat diffs as untrusted data and limit token permissions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review automation with an external AI service.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt smart test selection
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt test selection for these paths and commands: [mapping]. Validate matrix values and provide fallback behavior.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced CI optimization for a monorepo.

prompt_templates.title: Audit workflow security
prompt_templates.prompt: Harden this workflow: [workflow]. Check authorization, expression injection, secrets, outputs, action pinning, and rollback controls.

output_examples.input: Review an AI pull request workflow before deployment.
output: Restrict the job to trusted events and grant only required permissions.
Pass pull request content as data, redact secrets, and validate AI responses.
Pin every action to a reviewed commit SHA.

output_examples.input: Create issue triage for a small open-source repository.
output: Trigger on new issues and classify only against approved labels.
Request reproduction details when reports lack required information.
Require human review before assigning sensitive labels or closing issues.

best_practices: Grant each workflow only the permissions required by its job.
Treat repository text, filenames, comments, and AI output as untrusted data.
Test workflows in a restricted repository before enabling write operations.
anti_patterns: Do not interpolate GitHub context values directly into shell or JavaScript source.
Do not let public comments trigger privileged Git operations without authorization.
Do not send repository content to external AI services without review and redaction.

faq.question: Does this skill install workflows automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns that require adaptation, review, and repository installation.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Are the examples production ready?
faq.answer: No. Several examples need authorization, input handling, dependency pinning, and testing.

faq.question: Does it require GitHub secrets?
faq.answer: AI integrations require provider credentials. GitHub operations may also require a scoped token.

faq.question: Can it manage pull requests and issues?
faq.answer: Yes. The patterns cover reviews, comments, labels, stale items, and selected Git operations.

faq.question: Can it protect deployment decisions?
faq.answer: It can add risk checks, but sensitive deployments still require deterministic controls and human approval.
